en: I will send you the report by evening.
tamil: நான் சாயங்காலத்துக்குள்ள ரிப்போர்ட்டை உனக்கு அனுப்பிடுவேன்.
context: Promising a colleague you will share a document today.
explain: Use 'will' for a promise made now. 'By evening' means not later than evening.

en: Can we push the deadline to Friday?
tamil: டெட்லைனை வெள்ளிக்கிழமைக்கு தள்ளி வைக்கலாமா?
context: Asking your manager for more time on a task.
explain: 'Can we' is a polite way to ask. 'Push the deadline' means move it to a later date.

alt.en: Could we extend the deadline till Friday?

en: I am working on the presentation right now.
tamil: நான் இப்போ பிரசன்டேஷன் வேலையில இருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a colleague what you are busy with.
explain: Use 'am working' for something happening at this moment. 'Right now' stresses the present.

en: Did you check your email this morning?
tamil: இன்னைக்கு காலையில உன் மெயில் செக் பண்ணியா?
context: Asking a teammate if they saw an important message.
explain: Use 'did' with the base verb 'check' to ask about the past. 'This morning' gives the time.

en: My manager has already approved my leave.
tamil: என் மேனேஜர் ஏற்கனவே என் லீவை அப்ரூவ் பண்ணிட்டார்.
context: Telling a friend that your leave request is accepted.
explain: 'Has approved' shows an action finished with a result now. 'Already' means earlier than expected.

en: I need to take a day off tomorrow.
tamil: எனக்கு நாளைக்கு ஒரு நாள் லீவ் எடுக்கணும்.
context: Informing your boss you need leave.
explain: 'Need to' shows something necessary. 'Take a day off' means to be away from work for one day.

en: The meeting starts at ten sharp.
tamil: மீட்டிங் சரியா பத்து மணிக்கு ஆரம்பிக்கும்.
context: Reminding the team about the meeting time.
explain: We use the simple present for fixed schedules. 'Sharp' means exactly on time.

en: Please do not be late for the client call.
tamil: தயவு செஞ்சு கிளையன்ட் காலுக்கு லேட்டா வராதீங்க.
context: Warning teammates before an important call.
explain: 'Do not be' is a polite negative command. 'Please' makes it softer.

en: Who is handling this project?
tamil: இந்த ப்ராஜெக்ட்டை யார் பாத்துக்கிறாங்க?
context: Asking in a meeting who is in charge.
explain: 'Handling' here means managing or taking care of something. 'Who' asks about the person.

en: I could not open the attachment you sent.
tamil: நீங்க அனுப்புன அட்டாச்மென்ட்டை என்னால திறக்க முடியல.
context: Telling a sender their file did not open.
explain: 'Could not' is the past of 'cannot'. It tells us you were unable to do something.

en: Let us discuss this in tomorrow's meeting.
tamil: இதை நாளைக்கு மீட்டிங்ல பேசலாம்.
context: Postponing a topic to the next meeting.
explain: 'Let us' is used to make a suggestion for both of you. It sounds friendly and polite.

en: She will join our team next month.
tamil: அவங்க அடுத்த மாசம் நம்ம டீம்ல சேர்றாங்க.
context: Telling colleagues about a new team member.
explain: 'Will join' talks about a future event. 'Next month' tells us when.

en: I have been waiting for your reply since morning.
tamil: நான் காலையில இருந்து உங்க பதிலுக்காக காத்துக்கிட்டு இருக்கேன்.
context: Politely chasing someone for an answer.
explain: 'Have been waiting' shows an action that started in the past and continues now. 'Since' gives the starting point.

en: Could you share the meeting notes with me?
tamil: மீட்டிங் நோட்ஸை எனக்கு ஷேர் பண்ண முடியுமா?
context: Asking a colleague for notes you missed.
explain: 'Could you' is a very polite way to ask for something. 'Share with me' means send to me.

en: Our salary is credited on the last working day.
tamil: நம்ம சம்பளம் கடைசி வேலை நாள்ல வரவு வைக்கப்படும்.
context: Explaining the pay date to a new joiner.
explain: 'Is credited' is passive: the company puts money in your account. It is a regular fact, so we use the present.

en: I do not have access to that folder.
tamil: அந்த ஃபோல்டருக்கு எனக்கு அக்சஸ் இல்ல.
context: Telling the IT team about a permission problem.
explain: 'Do not have' shows you lack something. 'Access' means permission to open or use it.

en: Shall I book the conference room for you?
tamil: உங்களுக்காக கான்ஃபரன்ஸ் ரூமை நான் புக் பண்ணட்டுமா?
context: Offering to help a colleague organise a meeting.
explain: 'Shall I' is used to offer help politely. It is common in office English.

en: He is on leave until Monday.
tamil: அவர் திங்கட்கிழமை வரைக்கும் லீவ்ல இருக்கார்.
context: Telling a caller that a colleague is away.
explain: 'On leave' means away from work with permission. 'Until' shows the end time.

en: I finished the task before the deadline.
tamil: நான் டெட்லைனுக்கு முன்னாடியே வேலையை முடிச்சுட்டேன்.
context: Telling your manager you completed work early.
explain: 'Finished' is the simple past. 'Before the deadline' means earlier than the last date.

en: Why was the meeting cancelled?
tamil: மீட்டிங் ஏன் ரத்து பண்ணாங்க?
context: Asking a colleague about a sudden change.
explain: 'Was cancelled' is passive, so we do not say who cancelled it. 'Why' asks the reason.

en: We are not going to miss this target.
tamil: இந்த டார்கெட்டை நாம மிஸ் பண்ணப் போறதில்ல.
context: Motivating the team before a big deadline.
explain: 'Are not going to' is a firm way to talk about the future. 'Miss a target' means fail to reach it.
